title: Trailhead
description: A trip-planning app that turns a rough itinerary into a day-by-day map. Built to learn geospatial queries and get comfortable with caching.
longDescription: Trailhead started as a way to stop juggling five browser tabs every time I planned a trip. You drop in a rough list of places, and it works out a sensible day-by-day route, accounting for opening hours and travel time between stops. The backend indexes points of interest with PostGIS for fast nearest-neighbour queries, and the frontend caches route results so re-ordering a day doesn't mean waiting on the API again. Biggest lesson: geospatial indexing is a different mindset from typical relational queries, and it was worth the detour to learn it properly.

title: Understory
description: A markdown-first notes tool with local-first sync. Started as a weekend build, kept growing because I actually use it daily.
longDescription: Understory is a notes app for people who think in markdown. Everything is stored locally first using IndexedDB, so it works offline by default, and changes merge using a simple CRDT so the same notes stay consistent across a couple of devices without a central server owning the data. What began as a weekend experiment in local-first architecture is now the app I actually take notes in every day, which is the best sign a side project is worth continuing.

title: Canopy CLI
description: A small command-line tool for scaffolding React projects with sensible defaults, so new ideas take minutes to start, not hours.
longDescription: Canopy CLI is a scaffolding tool I built because I was tired of re-configuring the same Vite + ESLint + folder structure every time I started a new React idea. Written in Rust for a fast, dependency-free binary, it asks a handful of questions and generates a ready-to-run project in seconds. It taught me a lot about designing a good CLI interaction flow, and about Rust's file-system and templating ecosystem.
